description: Six trigger sequencers programmed as text, each row typed as the number of clocks from one trigger to the next.

params.text: Advances every row by one step.
Returns every row to the start of its pattern.
Forces that row to restart its pattern on the next clock, which is how a newly typed pattern takes effect without waiting for the old one to finish.

inputs.text: A trigger advances every row that has no cable in its own clock input.
A trigger returns every row that has no cable in its own reset input to the start of its pattern.
A trigger advances that row by one step, and a cable here makes the row ignore the global clock.
A trigger returns that row to the start of its pattern, and a cable here makes the row ignore the global reset.

outputs.text: Sends 10V on the steps that row's pattern calls for, with one polyphonic channel per pattern where the text sets more than one.
Sends a trigger on the first step of that row's pattern.

notes: a pattern is a string of step lengths: 2 triggers every second clock, 31 triggers on the 1st and 4th of every four, and 0 is a rest.
angle brackets hold a step length above 9, and @8 forces the pattern to repeat every 8 clocks whatever its own length is.
semicolons split a row into separate patterns for separate polyphonic channels, the hash character stands for the channel number, and arithmetic can be used wherever a length is expected.
a red display means a newly typed pattern is waiting for the running one to come back to its first step.
the six text fields start empty and no row sends anything until a pattern is typed into its field; click the field and type, for example 2 to trigger every second clock.
menu: Set All Channels Polyphony — sets every row's output to Automatic or to a fixed 1 to 16 channels.
Channel 1 Polyphony — sets that row's output to Automatic or to a fixed 1 to 16 channels; there is one such item per row, Channel 1 through Channel 6.
